name: Projection--Reduction Gluing for Maximum Parents
statement: For nonempty maximum-generated $H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X\sqcup D}$, put $U=\pi_XH$ and $I=\partial_DH$. Then $(U\times\{0\})\cup(I\times\{1\})$ is maximum-generated. If a supplied parent has rank $r$, marked auxiliary set $T$, $k=|D|$, $N=|X|+|T|$, and $0\le r-k<\min(r,N)$, a parent of rank $\min(r,N)$ retains the original mark and uses exactly $\min(r,N)-(r-k)-1\le k-1$ new auxiliaries.
proof: Successively reduce the parent on an initial part of $D$ and project the rest. The resulting nested classes on $X\sqcup T$ pass through consecutive maximum ranks from the full projection to the full reduction. Extend them to a maximum sequence. A delayed one-coordinate maximum sequence has entry levels zero and the rank gap at its two visible values; the disjoint level sum is a maximum parent whose marked section is exactly the two-shore gluing. Empty and equal endpoints reduce to constant-coordinate and product closure.
